title: Withdrawing a voluntary retirement application - is it allowed
p1:
Can an employee change their mind after applying for voluntary retirement? The answer may surprise many people.

A resignation-like decision is not always final the moment it is submitted.
p2: Many believe that once a voluntary retirement application is given, the employee has no option to take it back. But in many situations, withdrawal can be possible if it is done before the retirement becomes effective and before the employer has acted on it in a way that creates a final decision.
p3:
The key factor is timing. A voluntary retirement request is usually an offer by the employee, and whether it can be withdrawn depends on the applicable service rules, the terms of the scheme, and the stage at which the employer has accepted it.

The practical lesson: before submitting such an application, employees should carefully check the rules because reversing the decision later may not always be easy.
conclusion: Have you ever seen a case where an employee tried to withdraw a voluntary retirement request? Do you think employees should always get a chance to reconsider?
